Posh School Paedos [6213]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Alex Renton
One September day in the late 1960s, Alex Renton’s parents dropped him at Ashdown House in Sussex, one of the most elite boarding schools in the United Kingdom – it was the former preparatory school of Boris Johnson, Viscount Linley, the Queen’s nephew and actor Damian Lewis.
Alex was just eight years old, a little boy arriving at boarding school for the first time. A few hours later, Renton’s dormitory captain told the new boys that if they made the slightest noise after lights out, they would be whipped with a belt. Renton remembers lying with his pillow over his face, to “stifle the snuffles of homesickness”, while taking care not to move in case his bedsprings started to squeak. Beatings, bullying and cruelty were common. Later that year Alex was sexually abused by his maths and history teacher, Mr Keane.
“The teacher pulled me to his chest while he pushed his hand down the front of my corduroy shorts. It wasn’t wholly a surprise. I knew this could happen with Mr Keane, and that it was best to submit. He was violent: he liked to grab ears as well as penises, and would occasionally throw children who had annoyed him down the short flight of stairs that led from his classroom to the next. I also knew that when he’d finished his fumbling in your shorts, Mr Keane would give you a reward — a Rowntree’s Fruit Gum, to be precise.

At the end of 2013, Renton saw an article in the Daily Mail, which said that his old school was under investigation for historical sex abuse. When he read it he wept and realised that the teacher who abused him could still be abusing other children.
He wrote an essay about his abuse in The Observer. From that time on he started collecting hundreds of testimonies from other former boarding school pupils who said that they too had been beaten and abused.

“Neglect was — still is, perhaps — a part of the magic of the British boarding school system, admired and copied across the world. In my day, it went with violent discipline, dreadful food and the deliberate withdrawal of love at an early age — ingredients in the potion for turning us into fully functioning members of the ruling class. It is now abundantly clear that the system left the children of the privileged just as vulnerable to sadists and predatory paedophiles as were the occupants of Britain’s worst care homes and young offenders’ prisons. Those who ran the state institutions were accountable, the grand begowned men who ran the “great” schools were not. Or not until now.”

He has written a book, made a documentary and recently put out a series of podcasts titled “In Dark Corners”, referencing the places where the abuse took place.
The schools that have been implicated are the crème de la crème of British Education, Ashdown House, Eton College, Fettes, Aberlour and Gourdonstoun.
The allegations of abuse aren’t any different to the abuse stories that we have covered at schools in South Africa. Alex Renton calls it part of the colonial hangover.
The similarities are that the schools still want to protect their reputations and some of the parents are complicit, not allowing sexual abuse get in way of children’s academic and social progress.

What is of interest to South Africa is that two of the teachers who taught at Ashdown House have been charged with sexually abusing children, are retired and living in Cape Town.

DAVID PRICE RS-F5
British authorities want a former school teacher, who is in South Africa, to be extradited to face a swathe of sexual offence charges stretching from the 1970s to the 1990s. The offences Price is accused of were allegedly committed within the UK and do not relate to activities in South Africa. “Price is charged with 42 sexual offences of indecent assault against children and indecency with a child,” the application for extradition said. “Charges one to 33 relate to male pupils who attended Ashdown House School in East Sussex during the 1970s and 1980s when Price was employed as a teacher by the school. Charges 34 to 42 relate to male pupils who attended Brockhurst School in Berkshire during the 1980s and 1990s when similarly, Price was employed as a teacher by that school. “He later moved to his native South Africa where he taught at a school for the deaf for a decade until his retirement. During that time one of his pupils nominated him for Woolworths Teacher of the Year, a national award that he went on to win. After a year in retirement he became bored and found a job tutoring children privately until his arrest in November 2019 following an application by the British government. Price, who is single, was released on bail and lives at a retirement home in Cape Town which has a pre-school in its grounds. Its website states: ‘The children and elderly residents get together for super fun activities.’
https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2021-01-22-uk-wants-sa-to-extradite-ex-teacher-accused-of-indecently-assaulting-boys-from-the-1970s-to-1990s/

Iain Wares
Iain Wares was dismissed by a school in South Africa for indecent practises. He went to the UK and taught at Edinburgh Academy for 5 years and then he went to Fettes, Tony Blair’s former school.

20 former students have come forward recently and reported the sexual abuse to the police. While Edgar was at Fettes although parents complained the schools did not inform the police.

“Ben and Frank” abused by Wares
The boys had to stand next to him at desk and hold their jotters in their hands.
He told them to turn the pages and while they had their hands occupied, he would stroke the inside thighs, slap their buttocks and fondle their genitals.
One day EDGAR asked Frank wait for him after class. He slammed door and pushed Frank against the door and put his fingers in Frank’s anus.
People were walking nearby and Edgar stopped and shoved Frank out of the door.

Ben saw Frank extremely distressed; he was supported by two other boys in the corridor.
Frank’s mother set up a meeting. The headmaster said look into it. Frank’s mother was a doctor and knew how the system should work and that Edgar should be taken out of the educational system. But that is not what happened. What happened is recorded in minutes of a meeting.
The headmaster asked EDGAR if he sexually assault the boy and EDGAR did not deny it and it was taken as an admission. The headmaster Chenovix-Trench did not expel Edgar but gave him leave for a term to see a psychiatrist.
Chenovix -Trench decided not to report matter to police. After psych no reports of sexual abuse for about 3 years, Wares seemed calmer.

George Scott started two years after that and recalls that he was dragged by his hair off his chair to the cloakroom and beaten up by the teacher until he blacked out. Nothing was done about this either.
In January 1979 when another mother came to school gates to complain the board governors said go, but stay another 9 months. From there he came to South Africa and with an excellent reference taught at Bishops.
He is 82 years old now.

Although both teachers have cases against them they cannot be formally charged until they are on UK soil.

For decades Independent British boarding schools have earned a reputation for being amongst the finest education institutions in the world. Here some of the most notable minds were shaped, the likes of judges, politicians, captains of industry and aristocracy. Broadcaster, Nicky Campbell’s, parents believed it was a priceless gift.

Nicky
They just wanted the very best education and they sacrificed so much. I guess that's one of the reasons that we didn't say the stuff that was going on when we were little boys. We didn't want to let our parents down.

This prestigious education came at a cost, not only the prohibitive financial fees, but for the abused, an emotional toll from which they never recovered. Alex Renton is an author and journalist.

Alex
It's incredibly privileged education, which turns out to be which would set you up for life, as the parents were told. But it ended up being a life sentence.


V/O
At certain schools, beneath the veneer of privilege lurked a depraved underbelly, where children were used by adults for their own sexual gratification.

Nicky Campbell attended Edinburgh Academy. It is here he allegedly saw one of the accused,
Iain Wares, abuse his 10-year-old friend in the school’s changing rooms.

Nicky
And it's one of those images you can never unsee.

Mac
Do you have any recollection or can you still remember what happened on that day?

Nicky
This guy this teacher, he is standing over my friend, and he pulled my friends shorts down and fondling him and playing with his genitals.

Both teachers are resisting calls for justice; Wares’ says, due to his age, extradition would be too severe. Price argues he can’t be extradited because of Brexit.

Advocate. What would you say is the status of the extradition treaty between the UK and South Africa right now?

JJ
Now the UK from my information is still a member of the Council of Europe so the Extradition treaty is not affected in that way.

Advocate JJ du Toit who is the retired deputy director of Public Prosecutions and former head of the extradition desk, has a much clearer viewpoint.

You know, there is a misconception that they always must be a treaty between countries in order for them to extradite. It's not so there's an internationally recognized principle of comity, good neighbourliness. That is another avenue that is still available even for the sake of argument that there is no treaty.

In an affidavit, Iain Wares admits to abusing boys, he says his sexual tendencies were already evident in South Africa before he went to Scotland.

Link
After graduating at Cape Town University, Iain Wares came here to St George’s Grammar School in 1966.

V/O
The affidavit states “While I was teaching at St George’s Grammar School I sometimes had urges to touch the boys in an inappropriate manner.”

In 1967, he left South Africa to get psychiatric help for his problem in Scotland and he was admitted to the Royal Edinburgh Hospital for 3 months.

Link
But instead of staying away from children, Wares went on to get a teaching diploma and then got another teaching position at Edinburgh Academy.

And instead of urges, Iain Wares now acted upon his desires.





Nicky
You know, the pain is still there and the agony is still there. And the outrage is still there. And for many people, his hand is still there.

From Edinburgh Academy in Scotland to Ashdown House Preparatory School House in rural England. “Luke” is a businessman in his 50’s and was sent to board when was just 8 years old. He was at school with former Prime Minister Boris Johnson in the mid 70’s and King Charles’ III cousin, Viscount Linley was sent there a few years before.

Up Sound
Humane and beneficial to pupils.

But for Luke boarding school was utterly inhumane and he felt lonely and isolated.

Luke
So we had these holes in our hearts. We were incredibly vulnerable from being detached and taken away from our families, so we were looking for any adult who would give us attention.


V/O
They were tortuous years, Luke says he experienced 10 months of unrelenting abuse from his English teacher, South African, David Price, who groomed “chosen” boys and once he had won their trust, the abuse escalated from just touching to penetration.

Luke
The next thing I remember is I am lying down on his bed and he is pulling my shorts down and he is touching my penis. So next stage of memory was um then having a pain in my anus, and I don’t know if it was something else but I assume that I was penetrated digitally.










V/O
Alex Renton was the 8th generation in his family to go to boarding school. Like Luke, he too attended Ashdown House Preparatory School.

Alex
It was the British model that produced people to go and rule the empire and the ethos was hardship, teaching resilience, violent discipline. And that, of course, is an environment that is very good for predatory paedophiles. You know, vulnerable children in an atmosphere where secrets must be kept.

V/O
And the cultivation of secrets is part of the paedophile’s arsenal.
Alex Renton was abused at the age of 9 and the teacher gave him a sweet as compensation afterwards.
When his mother heard of this she challenged the headmaster. But the headmaster then accused her son of making it up.

Alex
And I in the headmaster’s eyes. I was the filthy boy, a filthy minded boy. And that's what he called me in public for the next four years.
Well, what, you know, I found most troubling as I grew up was those four years of psychological abuse by the headmaster, a man who should have been protecting me.

Up Sound
Presenter
How would you like it to be remembered?
Headmaster
As the 5 happiest years of their life?

V/O
Luke says it was sheer hell, when he told the Headmaster that David Price was abusing him, it was ignored and the abuser became the tormentor.

Luke
The most terrifying thought came to me, I have told the most powerful person there is and he can’t protect me. The sexual abuse stopped but the psychological and emotional abuse continued from both of them for 2 more years they were the most terrifying two years of my life.

Severe corporal punishment and sexual abuse was so rife in boarding schools and care homes, that in 2015 the United Kingdom set up a number of inquiries. Hundreds of victims came forward to give testimony of the exploitation they suffered at the hands of numerous perpetrators.

Up sound
We want to hear from every single person who comes within our remit and wants to tell us about being abused.

When Luke and Alex Renton testified, they felt that it was the first time the “adults” had actually listened to them.

So these inquiries shone a very strong light into these dark fetid corners of English and Scottish society.

To create awareness of the scourge of abuse, Alex Renton used his influence as a journalist and has bravely spoken about his abuse in articles and podcasts, in 2018 he made a documentary in which he revisited Ashdown House.

John Snow
What does it feel like being here?

Alex
Bloody horrible. It’s a sunny day in a beautiful place and I was very unhappy here for too long for a small child and it took me too long to get over it.

With all of the media attention, Alex Renton says that over 1000 people have written to him with similar stories of abuse. He holds the schools accountable.

Alex
If they did have to get rid of the teacher because too many parents and children had complained, they didn't tell the police.

They gave them a reference and enabled them to get go get a job at another school.

Link
When the doors of teaching closed in the UK, both Price And Wares returned to South Africa. David Price taught here at Western Province Prep School for about 14 years.

V/O
And Wares taught at Rondebosch Boys’ Prep School for 27 years and says he never abused again.

Bronagh Hammond at the Western Cape Education Department says Price and Wares’ records in South Africa are clean.

Mac
Obviously, said another official level, nothing has been put forward. You've got no records whatsoever.

Bronagh
No records whatsoever. And we have checked with the schools involved and to ask them if they have any history of any records against them. And they have also confirmed that they cannot find any evidence.

Alex, Nicky & Luke may have been protected if the UK had made it compulsory to report any suspicion of abuse to an outside authority. These three are now supporting a campaign to make that legally enforceable.

We will go on having these problems until we get the law correct, if the law had been right when X abused you and your friends they would have been stopped that year. And it’s unbelievable that you know 40 years after we were at school children are still at risk in that way.

Mac
What is the department’s stance on abuse right now?

Bronagh
It’s mandatory now under the Children's Act and the Criminal Law Act for someone to actually report there, it has been a disclosure of child abuse to actually reported. And then they are actually criminally negligent if they do not do so.

V/O
The psychological toll of abuse is well known. It’s a weight that Luke has carried for over 40 years and he admits that he spent a lot of time in therapy just learning how to trust again. He tracked David Price down twenty years ago by hiring a private investigator who told him that he was in South Africa and teaching.

Mac

My anger at the original school was just huge. But very likely, given the nature of the man to abused children in South Africa.

Alex
We should be partly ashamed for allowing these men, these dangerous men, to be exported to South Africa. But I do wonder at what point South Africa is going to get it together to. Make sure justice is done and give the survivors in back in UK the closure they need.

V/O
What Alex is talking about is extradition. David Price’s matter is still pending in court and there is no hearing date yet. Carte Blanche wanted his side of the story.

David Price
I am old, ok 76 and I can’t think clearly at the moment. You are putting pressure on me.

Mac
Are you saying that you have never sexually abused any boys at any stage at any time that you have been teaching?

David Price
Right.

Mac
I hope he gets his day in court.

Between


Link
Many people feels that Wares gets to spend the rest of his days in comfort in a retirement village in Fish Hoek Cape Town. But his victims are still suffering from the psychological trauma of his abuse.

Nicky
He is living in comfortable retirement while many of these men of my age have been living with a nightmare.

Up Sound
Hi, No cameras. We are here to see Iain Wares. No cameras.

Carte Blanche went to Wares’s home, looking for answers.

Man
I have spoken to him he says he doesn’t wish to chat to you guys at all.

Mac
Doesn’t want to chat. OK.

When asked the Justice Ministry would not confirm if the extradition treaty between South Africa and Britain was still in place as it was part of this litigation.
What is certain is that the victims are still waiting for justice.

Mac
What would it mean for you if Wares were to end up in court and finally face up to all of these allegations and charges?

Nicky
If he were to be extradited, and face trial, at least those little boys would feel vindicated.
Justice is release. That is what justice is, the first day of the rest of our life.

metadata.Further information: Alex Renton One September day in the late 1960s, Alex Renton’s parents dropped him at Ashdown House in Sussex, one of the most elite boarding schools in the United Kingdom – it was the former preparatory school of Boris Johnson, Viscount Linley, the Queen’s nephew and actor Damian Lewis. Alex was just eight years old, a little boy arriving at boarding school for the first time. A few hours later, Renton’s dormitory captain told the new boys that if they made the slightest noise after lights out, they would be whipped with a belt. Renton remembers lying with his pillow over his face, to “stifle the snuffles of homesickness”, while taking care not to move in case his bedsprings started to squeak. Beatings, bullying and cruelty were common. Later that year Alex was sexually abused by his maths and history teacher, Mr Keane. “The teacher pulled me to his chest while he pushed his hand down the front of my corduroy shorts. It wasn’t wholly a surprise. I knew this could happen with Mr Keane, and that it was best to submit. He was violent: he liked to grab ears as well as penises, and would occasionally throw children who had annoyed him down the short flight of stairs that led from his classroom to the next. I also knew that when he’d finished his fumbling in your shorts, Mr Keane would give you a reward — a Rowntree’s Fruit Gum, to be precise. At the end of 2013, Renton saw an article in the Daily Mail, which said that his old school was under investigation for historical sex abuse. When he read it he wept and realised that the teacher who abused him could still be abusing other children. He wrote an essay about his abuse in The Observer. From that time on he started collecting hundreds of testimonies from other former boarding school pupils who said that they too had been beaten and abused. “Neglect was — still is, perhaps — a part of the magic of the British boarding school system, admired and copied across the world. In my day, it went with violent discipline, dreadful food and the deliberate withdrawal of love at an early age — ingredients in the potion for turning us into fully functioning members of the ruling class. It is now abundantly clear that the system left the children of the privileged just as vulnerable to sadists and predatory paedophiles as were the occupants of Britain’s worst care homes and young offenders’ prisons. Those who ran the state institutions were accountable, the grand begowned men who ran the “great” schools were not. Or not until now.” He has written a book, made a documentary and recently put out a series of podcasts titled “In Dark Corners”, referencing the places where the abuse took place. The schools that have been implicated are the crème de la crème of British Education, Ashdown House, Eton College, Fettes, Aberlour and Gourdonstoun. The allegations of abuse aren’t any different to the abuse stories that we have covered at schools in South Africa. Alex Renton calls it part of the colonial hangover. The similarities are that the schools still want to protect their reputations and some of the parents are complicit, not allowing sexual abuse get in way of children’s academic and social progress. What is of interest to South Africa is that two of the teachers who taught at Ashdown House have been charged with sexually abusing children, are retired and living in Cape Town.
